newsitem.title: FRANCE: French doctors check sect children after boy dies.
newsitem.headline: French doctors check sect children after boy dies.

text.p: A dozen doctors, aided by police, examined and found healthy some 75 children on Monday in the homes of a sect in southwest France after a 19-month-old boy died from lack of medical care, police said.
After the examinations, a public prosecutor said the children bore no signs of physical abuse.
Police raided two farms owned by the U.S.-based Tabitha's Place sect in Angous and Sus, near Pau, in the early morning.

Sect members Raphael Ginoux, 36, and his German-born wife Dagmar were remanded in custody at the weekend and put under investigation on suspicion of failing to give their son Raphael adequate care, after he died on Thursday from malnutrition and an untreated heart ailment.
"In the case of Raphael last week we discovered documents concerning the community which advocate corporal punishment," said state prosecutor Jean-Pierre Dreno.
"We figured people were being mistreated and that's why we're here today," he told reporters.
Investigators said some 100 adults and 70 children lived at the farms in total isolation from the outside world, refusing outside medical care and teaching their children at home.
